t: #3585 Find Weighted Median Node in Tree
o: For each query (u, v) we walk the unique tree path and must return the first node x with dist(u, x) >= totalPathWeight / 2. With n, q up to 1e5 we need per-query logarithmic time: binary lifting for LCA and weighted ancestor jumps. Split the path at the LCA w; depending on whether half the total weight is reached within the u-to-w leg, the median lies on one leg or the other, and each leg is a chain of ancestors amenable to binary lifting.
k: Compute LCA w, du = dist(u,w), dv = dist(w,v), T = du + dv with binary lifting.
If 2*du >= T, the median is on the u-leg: lift from u to the deepest node with 2*dist(u,x) < T and answer its parent.
Otherwise it is on the v-leg: lift from v to the deepest ancestor y with 2*dist(v,y) <= 2*du + 2*dv - T.
All comparisons use doubled distances to stay in integers.

a.i: Precompute up[k][v] and sum[k][v] (ancestor 2^k levels up and accumulated weight). The path decomposes at the LCA into two vertical chains; on each chain the distance from the endpoint is monotone, so a greedy binary descent finds the boundary node in O(log n).
s: Root the tree at 0, build depth/parent/weight tables and binary lifting arrays iteratively.
Per query, find LCA w and du, dv via lifting sums.
If 2*du >= T: descend from u keeping 2*dist < T and depth >= depth(w); return parent of the landing node.
Else descend from v keeping 2*dist(v,y) <= 2*du+2*dv-T and depth >= depth(w); return the landing node.
a.t: O((n + q) log n) — building lifting tables is O(n log n), each query O(log n).
a.sp: O(n log n) for the binary lifting tables.

w: Everything reduces to monotone searches on two vertical chains after splitting at the LCA. Pitfalls: off-by-one on the strict vs non-strict comparison (use doubled integers: 2*dist < T for the pre-median, <= for the limit on the v-side), forgetting u == v, and restricting lifts to depth >= depth(LCA). Follow-up: handle dynamic edge weights (link-cut trees) or median by vertex count instead of weight.
